issues.display_title: Issue #1988: fix(paypal): Harden PayPal subscription endpoints against DoS, SQL wildcard scan, and concurrency race conditions
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Security and performance audit on /paypal/subscriptions and /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/status-stream identified several vulnerabilities and stability risks:

  1. Worker Starvation (DoS Risk): SSE stream holds a synchronous PHP worker process for up to 60 seconds with per-second blocking loop.
  2. SQL Wildcard & Cross-Tenant Leak: GetSubscriptionStatusStream performs note LIKE "%{$subscriptionId}%" without input format validation, allowing wildcard % inputs to match arbitrary completed transactions and triggering 1-second interval Full Table Scans.
  3. Upgrade/Downgrade Race Condition: Lack of atomic mutex lock during concurrent upgrade/downgrade requests allows duplicate PayPal subscription creation with duplicated proration discounts.
  4. Auth User ID Extraction: CreateSubscription inspects $request->input('user_id') before $request->user_id injected by the auth middleware.

Proposed Changes

  1. GetSubscriptionStatusStream.php:
    • Enforce strict PayPal Subscription ID regex validation (/^I-[A-Z0-9_-]{8,30}$/i), rejecting invalid inputs with HTTP 400 before DB access.
    • Remove per-second LIKE '%...%' Full Table Scan queries from inside the streaming loop; inside loop only check Redis fast cache. Initial DB check uses exact match (profile_id = ?).
  2. CreateSubscription.php:
    • Completely eliminate $request->input('user_id'). Strictly resolve user identity from $request->user_id injected by auth middleware.
    • Add Redis distributed lock (SET NX EX 20) on paypal:lock:sub_action:{userId} during upgrade and downgrade operations.
    • Fallback buildCallbackUrl to safe configured domain instead of untrusted host headers.

Target Project Board

  • Added to Project Board #43 (GoThru API - Development) with status To Do.

Result

  • Pull Request: #1989
  • Branch: fix/harden-paypal-subscription-endpoints-1988
  • Key Commits:
    • 1b3078e5b — Initial hardening & tests
    • f3c2a84a5 — Completely eliminate body user_id in favor of auth middleware
  • Modified Files:
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/GetSubscriptionStatusStream.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/GetSubscriptionStatus.php
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/CreateSubscription.php
    • tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/PaypalSubscriptionHardeningTest.php
  • Test Evidence:
    • PaypalSubscriptionHardeningTest.php: 6 tests, 44 assertions, 100% pass rate.
    • CreateSubscriptionBuyStorageTest.php: 3 tests, 18 assertions, 100% pass rate.
    • PaypalWebhookVerificationTest.php: 8 tests, 25 assertions, 100% pass rate.

issues.display_title: Issue #1990: refactor(paypal): remove obsolete and unused PayPal API routes and action handlers
issues.main_description_html:
Background

During the recent PayPal subscription security and architecture audit, we analyzed the active endpoint consumption between gothru-dashboard:master (frontend) and GoThru-API-New:main (backend).

We identified 20 unused/obsolete endpoints and action classes in the backend. These routes were originally created as general PayPal API wrappers, but:

  1. Neither gothru-dashboard nor any internal service in GoThru-API-New (cron jobs, queue workers, or controllers) ever invokes them.
  2. Official cancellation is handled securely via POST /v2/payment/subscription/unsubscribe (binding user identity from DB without IDOR).
  3. Plan and product catalogs are managed internally within GoThru's database rather than via client-facing PayPal product/plan endpoints.
  4. Keeping these orphaned endpoints introduces unnecessary attack surfaces (such as missing role checks on plan deactivation and IDOR risks on direct subscription cancellation).

Scope of Work

1. Route Definitions to Remove (routes/paypalRoutes.php)

  • Subscriptions group (7 endpoints):
    • GET /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}
    • PATCH /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}
    • POST /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/revise
    • POST /paypal/subscriptions/handle-approval
    • POST /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/suspend
    • POST /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/cancel
    • POST /paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/activate
  • Plans group (6 endpoints):
    • POST /paypal/plans
    • GET /paypal/plans
    • GET /paypal/plans/{planId}
    • PATCH /paypal/plans/{planId}
    • POST /paypal/plans/{planId}/activate
    • POST /paypal/plans/{planId}/deactivate
  • Products group (4 endpoints):
    • POST /paypal/products
    • GET /paypal/products
    • GET /paypal/products/{productId}
    • PUT /paypal/products/{productId}
  • Orders group (2 endpoints):
    • GET /paypal/orders/{orderId}
    • POST /paypal/orders/{orderId}/authorize
  • Public testing endpoint (1 endpoint):
    • POST /paypal/webhook-test

2. Controller & Action Classes Cleanup

  • Remove corresponding unused methods in app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/PaypalController.php.
  • Remove dead action classes in:
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Subscription/ (CancelSubscription.php, SuspendSubscription.php, ActivateSubscription.php, ReviseSubscription.php, UpdateSubscription.php, ShowSubscription.php, HandleUpgradeApproval.php)
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Plan/ (all 6 files)
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Subscription/Product/ (all 4 files)
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/ (ShowOrder.php, AuthorizeOrder.php)

3. Documentation & Router Integrity Test

  • Sync docs/REGISTERED_APIS.md to reflect active registered routes.
  • Update tests/Routes/DeadRoutesCleanedIntegrityTest.php to assert all remaining routes resolve to valid controller methods and verify deleted routes are not registered.

Acceptance Criteria

  • All 20 obsolete routes are removed from routes/paypalRoutes.php.
  • Active routes (/orders, /orders/capture, /overlay-orders, /orders/capture-overlay, /subscriptions, /subscriptions/capture, /subscriptions/{id}/status-stream, /webhooks) remain untouched and functional.
  • No regression on existing PayPal subscription, webhook, or checkout unit tests.
  • DeadRoutesCleanedIntegrityTest passes with 100% integrity.

Result

  • Pull Request: #1991
  • Branch: refactor/cleanup-paypal-dead-routes-1990
  • Key Commit: 0c72553c9
  • Modified & Deleted Files:
    • routes/paypalRoutes.php: 20 obsolete routes removed (9 active routes retained).
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/PaypalController.php: Removed all unused methods and unused action imports.
    • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/: Deleted 19 dead action classes and 2 unused folders (Subscription/Plan/, Subscription/Product/).
    • docs/REGISTERED_APIS.md: Updated total routes from 682 to 662 routes.
    • tests/Routes/DeadRoutesCleanedIntegrityTest.php: Added assertions confirming all 20 removed routes are not registered and all remaining routes have valid controller methods.
  • Verification & Test Results:
    • DeadRoutesCleanedIntegrityTest: 2 tests, 37 assertions, 100% PASS.
    • PaypalSubscriptionHardeningTest: 6 tests, 44 assertions, 100% PASS.
    • PaypalWebhookVerificationTest: 8 tests, 25 assertions, 100% PASS.

issues.display_title: Issue #1992: feat(analytics): implement server-side Countly tracking for payment webhooks and lifecycle events
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Migrate terminal payment and financial outcome tracking from the frontend to the backend. In accordance with the "Webhook-First & Server as Single Source of Truth" architecture, financial captures, subscription revisions, and payment denials must be authoritative and tracked directly from gateway webhooks (PayPal & Stripe).

Scope & Objectives

  1. Countly Ingestion Service:

    • Create a dedicated service/client (CountlyService.php) in Laravel using Http::post() targeting Countly's /i ingestion endpoint.
    • Configure environment variables in .env and config/services.php:
      • COUNTLY_HOST (e.g. https://data.gothru.org)
      • COUNTLY_APP_KEY
    • Implement asynchronous/queued event emission or resilient timeout handling to prevent blocking webhook responses.

  2. Instrument Webhook & Lifecycle Handlers:

    • Emit payment_completed:
      • When PayPal PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED or CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED webhook is verified and captured.
      • When Stripe payment intent or charge succeeds.
    • Emit payment_failed:
      • When PayPal PAYMENT.SALE.DENIED webhook is received.
      • When Stripe payment intent / dunning detects failure.
    • Emit subscription_changed & subscription_change_failed:
      • Inside PayPal/Stripe upgrade, downgrade, and plan modification processors.

  3. Privacy & Security Constraints:

    • Maintain strict Zero-PII policy: Do not send credit card numbers, billing addresses, payer emails, or raw database IDs.
    • Send only sanitized metadata: payment_type, payment_provider, plan_code, action, and normalized reason_code.

  4. Testing & Verification:

    • Unit and Feature tests with mocked HTTP client (Http::fake()) verifying Countly payload structure and non-blocking webhook processing.

Result

  • Pull Request: #1994
  • Branch: feat/countly-server-side-tracking-1992
  • Key Implementation Files:
    • Service: app/Services/Analytics/CountlyService.php
    • Config: config/countly.php, bootstrap via bootstrap/app.php
    • Webhook & Payment Handlers:
      • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php
      • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php
      • app/Actions/Payment/Paypal/UpgradeIntentProcessor.php
      • app/Actions/Payment/Paypal/DowngradeIntentProcessor.php
      • app/Actions/Payment/Paypal/BuyStorageIntentProcessor.php
      • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/SubscriptionHelpers.php
      • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/PaymentHelpers.php
      • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/StripeFailedPaymentDetector.php
      • Stripe Action Handlers (Upgrade, CompleteUpgrade3DS, Downgrade, SpaceAddon, CompleteSpaceAddon3DS)
  • Testing Evidence:
    • tests/Unit/Services/CountlyServiceTest.php: 9 tests, 59 assertions, 100% pass rate.
    • tests/Unit/Payment/PaymentWebhookCountlyTrackingTest.php: 4 tests, 6 assertions, 100% pass rate.

issues.display_title: Issue #1996: feat(support): implement Countly analytics read and aggregation API for Support dashboard
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Implement a secure backend aggregation API in GoThru-API-New that interfaces with Countly's Read API (/o or /o/analytics) to provide high-level product, session traffic, and financial analytics data for the Support / Admin dashboard.

Scope & Objectives

  1. Countly Read API Client / Service Method:

    • Extend CountlyService (or implement dedicated CountlyReadService) to query Countly's REST Read API (/o/analytics/dashboard or /o queries).
    • Use configured host (COUNTLY_HOST) and read credentials (COUNTLY_API_KEY, COUNTLY_APP_KEY).
    • Implement query methods for:
      • Traffic & session overview (total users, new users, sessions, session duration).
      • Event metrics & breakdowns (total counts and time-series for payment events like payment_completed, payment_failed, subscription_changed, and lifecycle events like tour_created, panorama_upload_completed).
    • Implement response caching (e.g. 5–15 minutes TTL) to optimize latency and prevent rate-limiting Countly server.

  2. Support API Endpoint:

    • Register endpoint: GET /v2/support/analytics/countly (under v2/support prefix).
    • Require authentication and authorization: Support / Admin role only (user_type == '2').
    • Accept query parameters:
      • period (e.g. 7d, 30d, 90d, custom)
      • start_date and end_date (optional ISO date format for custom ranges)
      • metrics (optional filter for specific metrics: events, users, payments)

  3. Privacy & Security Constraints:

    • Enforce Zero-PII: No raw user emails, credit cards, or internal user identifiers exposed in public/analytics payloads.
    • Aggregate numbers only (counts, percentages, sums).

  4. Testing & Verification:

    • Unit tests covering Countly read queries, caching logic, and error resilience when Countly is unreachable.
    • Controller / Feature tests validating permission checks (403 for non-support users, 200 for support role).

Result

  • Pull Request: #1998
  • Branch: feat/support-countly-analytics-api-1996
  • Commit: 875a81508
  • Key Implementation Files:
    • Config: config/countly.php (api_key, app_id, read_timeout, cache_ttl)
    • Domain Service: app/Services/Analytics/CountlyReadService.php

    • Controller: app/Http/Controllers/Support/CountlyAnalyticsController.php
    • Route: routes/supportRoutes.php (GET /v2/support/analytics/countly)

    • tests/Unit/Support/GetCountlyAnalyticsFlowTest.php: 4 tests, 7 assertions, 100% pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #1997: refactor(internal): prune internal virtual tours response to essential properties with thumbnail and overlay status
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Currently, the internal virtual tours provider endpoint (GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours) executes a SELECT * query on the hosted_tours.tours table, returning 35+ columns per item. Most of these fields are internal database scheduling flags and schema artifacts (e.g. 1_cid, goverlay_activate_date, fschedule_deactivate_at, koverlay_active, xml_version, payed_download) that pollute the response payload, leak internal database structures, and lack a direct panorama thumbnail URL required by caller applications (Panorra, Villume) for their asset picker modals.

Proposed Changes

Refactor InternalVirtualTourRepository and response transformation for GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours to strictly filter and map the return data to the agreed essential contract:

  1. Selective Field Extraction:
    Restrict the returned item attributes strictly to:

    • tour_id (int): Tour identifier.
    • tour_key (string): Unique tour key identifier.
    • tour_name (string): Human-readable tour title.
    • lat (string|null): Latitude coordinate.
    • lng (string|null): Longitude coordinate.
    • 1_cid (string): Direct CID key as stored in database.
    • thumbnail (string): CDN thumbnail image URL (https://img.gothru.org/...) resolved from panorama assets, or empty string "" if not available.
    • goverlay_active (string): Google overlay active status flag ("0", "1", "2", "3").
    • foverlay_active (string): Free/hosted overlay active status flag ("0", "1", "2", "3").

  2. Thumbnail Resolution:

    • Resolve thumbnail URLs efficiently in batch for the paginated page (max 20-100 items) using 4_panoramas.thumb_local_path without N+1 overhead.

  3. Prune Internal Schema Fields:

    • Eliminate all extraneous columns: moderation_id, xml_version, cdn, share_key, stats_key, auto_links, whitelable, favicon, matamo, api_key_id, deactivated*, has_json, type, and all overlay scheduling timestamps (*schedule_*_at, *overlay_activate_date).

  4. Search and Status Filtering:

    • Support keyword search via tour_name, tour_key, and 1_cid.
    • Support optional goverlay_active and foverlay_active status filters supporting single values as well as comma-separated multi-values (e.g. 1,2).

  5. Update Tests & Documentation:

    • Update InternalVirtualTourRepositoryTest and GetUserVirtualToursInternalControllerTest asserting the exact allowed response keys, filter parameters, and status validations.
    • Update docs/v2/tours/management/internal-user-virtual-tours.md.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Endpoint GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours returns only the 9 specified properties per tour item in data.
  • Retain 1_cid key directly from database.
  • thumbnail returns valid CDN image URL or empty string.
  • Supports search via tour_name, tour_key, and 1_cid.
  • Supports optional multi-status filtering via goverlay_active and foverlay_active (single or comma-separated).
  • Pagination envelope (total, page, per_page, total_pages) remains intact.
  • Unit & Feature tests pass with 100% assertions covering the trimmed response structure and filters.

Result

  • Pull Request: #1999 (refactor/prune-internal-virtual-tours-1997 - Merged to main via 509d3098c)
  • Key Commits:
    • 4badb7b26: Initial prune to 9 properties with CDN thumbnail resolution.
    • 03160d057: API contract and payload specification documentation.
    • ac6c2033a: Keyword search support for 1_cid.
    • e605fbb6b: Retain 1_cid key name as-is from database.
    • 0fd738b93: Support goverlay_active and foverlay_active query filters.
    • 909868787: Support comma-separated multi-values for overlay filters (1,2 etc.).
  • Files Modified:
    • app/Repositories/Internal/InternalVirtualTourRepository.php: Implemented selective query projection, batch thumbnail resolver, 1_cid search, and overlay multi-status filters (whereIn).
    • app/Http/Controllers/Internal/GetUserVirtualToursInternalController.php: Query parameter parsing, multi-value validation (0,1,2,3), and 400 Bad Request error handling.
    • docs/v2/tours/management/internal-user-virtual-tours.md: Comprehensive API documentation including parameters, headers, data structures, and curl examples.
    • tests/Repositories/Internal/InternalVirtualTourRepositoryTest.php: Tests for 9 properties, CDN resolution, and single/multiple overlay filters.
    • tests/Http/Controllers/Internal/GetUserVirtualToursInternalControllerTest.php: Feature tests for pagination, search, overlay filtering, and validation error cases.
  • Verification & Test Pass Rates:
    • InternalVirtualTourRepositoryTest.php: 10 tests, 50 assertions passed (100%).
    • GetUserVirtualToursInternalControllerTest.php: 15 tests, 36 assertions passed (100%).
    • KeycloakServiceAuthMiddlewareTest.php: 13 tests, 42 assertions passed (100%).

issues.display_title: Issue #2000: feat(internal): support overlay active status filters and 1_cid search on virtual tours endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Following the response pruning on GET /internal/users/{uuid}/virtual-tours (Issue #1997), consumer applications (Panorra, Villume, GoThru Portal) need capability to filter virtual tours based on active overlay statuses (Google overlay vs Hosted overlay) and search tours directly by their customer/place identifier (1_cid).

Key Requirements & Additions

  1. 1_cid Key & Search Integration:

    • Retain 1_cid key name as-is from database structure.
    • Extend keyword search (?search=...) to query against 1_cid in addition to tour_name and tour_key.

  2. Overlay Status Filtering (goverlay_active & foverlay_active):

    • Provide optional query parameters:
      • goverlay_active: Filter by Google overlay status (0, 1, 2, 3).
      • foverlay_active: Filter by Hosted overlay status (0, 1, 2, 3).
    • Support multiple comma-separated values (e.g. goverlay_active=1,2&foverlay_active=0,3).
    • Default behavior: when omitted, return all virtual tours regardless of overlay status (backward-compatible).
    • Strict validation: return HTTP 400 Bad Request if any value outside 0, 1, 2, 3 is supplied.

  3. Documentation & Testing:

    • Update contract documentation in docs/v2/tours/management/internal-user-virtual-tours.md.
    • Add unit and feature test coverage for single and comma-separated filter combinations.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Query param search matches substrings in tour_name, tour_key, and 1_cid.
  • Query params goverlay_active and foverlay_active accept single and comma-separated values (0, 1, 2, 3).
  • Invalid values trigger HTTP 400 with a descriptive error message.
  • When filter params are omitted, all active tours are returned as default.
  • Unit & Feature tests pass with 100% assertions.

Result

  • Key Commits:
    • ac6c2033a: feat(internal): support search by cid on internal virtual tours endpoint
    • e605fbb6b: fix(tours): retain 1_cid key as-is from database in internal virtual tours response
